title: Allied Blenders and Distillers Ltd - 544203 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Record FY26 EBITDA ₹568 crore (14.4% margin) driven by premium mix and pricing, but management guides only flat FY27 margins with Q1 pressure, and supply-side evidence is largely capex-led backward integration rather than capacity discipline.

summary.headline: Q4 FY26 EBITDA rose 21.2% to a record ₹182 crore with margin up 179 bps to 17.9%; FY27 margins guided flat to FY26 at 14.4%.
summary.overview: Consolidated income from operations for Q4 FY26 was ₹1,020 crore, up 9.1% YoY, with P&A volume up 20.5% to 4.4 million cases. Gross margin expanded 480 bps YoY to 48.2%, partly reinvested in brand-building. For FY26, consolidated revenue grew 11.5% to ₹3,949 crore, EBITDA rose 25.8% to ₹568 crore and reported PAT was ₹220 crore (adjusted ₹266 crore after ₹45.45 crore of tax items). Management guided FY27 mid-teens top-line growth, with a Q1 and early Q2 margin squeeze from the West Asia conflict before recovery from FTA, Telangana price hike and backward integration.

segments.name: P&A (Prestige & Above)
segments.commentary: Q4 volume up 20.5% YoY to 4.4 million cases, 57.7% of sales. FY26 share was 47.2% of volume and 57.3% of value. ICONiQ White sold 10.7 million cases in FY26 (up about 88%).

segments.name: Mass premium and other
segments.commentary: Q4 volume up 5.6% QoQ, driven by South and East, but flat YoY as management prioritised profitable state brand mix. Officer's Choice brandy has begun in Andhra Pradesh.

segments.name: ABD Maestro (super premium to luxury)
segments.commentary: Launched 10 brands, now in about 11 states and 4 travel retail locations. FY27 target to cross ₹100 crore revenue; year 1 EBITDA negative.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: FY26 export revenue up 14.1% to ₹235 crore; markets rose from 23 to 36. Q4 was partly hit by geopolitical disruption.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated top-line growth guided to mid-teens, in line with stated guidelines.
P&A expected to grow at high teens by FY28; mass premium and other to grow low to mid-single digits.
FY27 overall EBITDA margin guided to be at least equal to FY26 (14.4%); Q1 and early Q2 to see margin pressure from West Asia conflict.
Phase 1 and 2 backward integration expected to add about 300 bps to EBITDA margin by FY28 and about 100 bps more by FY29; FY28 EBITDA margin target raised to 18% from 17%.
UK FTA expected in Q2 FY27; Telangana price increase planned for H2 FY27 base case.
Management expects leverage to stay within guardrails on an annualised basis through the capex cycle; does not intend to breach covenants.
ESOP charge of about ₹5-6 crore per quarter in FY27.
capex_capacity: Phase 1 PET bottling facility in Telangana commissioned in Q2 FY26 and EBITDA accretive from Q3; it meets about 70-75% of requirement.
Malt distillery in Telangana (4 million litres, 12 KLPD per Amar Sinha) expected operational in H1 FY27.
ENA distillery expansion in Maharashtra expected operational in H1 FY28.
Phase 2 backward integration covers bottling and ENA in Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra and Andhra Pradesh; UP bottling plant expected in H2 to avoid ₹27 franchise fee on own brands.
Accelerated depreciation on certain plant assets, including the PET facility, raised Q4 and FY26 depreciation.
demand_pricing: Telangana: receivables and overdue receivables fell QoQ in Q4; management says FY24 and FY25 dues are cleared. Telangana price increase committee formed; management hopes for Q2 but plans for H2.
Karnataka: slab reduction policy not yet implemented; management sees neutral to positive for Officer's Choice (about 300,000 cases a year), with ICONiQ a potential opportunity.
Price increases taken in several markets; management says gross margin gain came from price, trade-spend control, state brand mix and about 30 bps from PET unit.
The Prestige & Above whisky segment is about 120 million cases, with ICONiQ, OC Blue and SRB7 at about 18-20 million cases combined. Management acknowledges some cannibalisation.
OC Blue and SRB7 are over 10 years old; SRB7 test marketing showed low single-digit growth. OC Blue packaging refresh due Q2 FY27.
CSD industry size about 12 million cases a year; ICONiQ, SRB7, Kyron and Jolly Roger approved. Management says ABD Maestro's 1% volume share equals about 9% value.

qa_highlights.question: How much FY27 margin upside from UK FTA, Telangana price hike and backward integration, and will H1 margins hold given glass and fuel inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 margins to be broadly equal to FY26, with pressure in Q1 and early Q2 and expansion from H2. Telangana hike is seen as a significant upside.

qa_highlights.question: Amar Sinha's vision and leadership transition timing?
qa_highlights.answer: He outlined a 3-year plan: premium-and-above above 50% of volume, high-teens revenue growth, 48-50% gross margin, EBITDA margin above 20% and ROCE about 25%. Alok Gupta said the transition announcement is expected within this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ICONiQ expansion plan and ABD Maestro ARR?
qa_highlights.answer: ICONiQ is distributed nationally, approved in CSD, and exported to 9 countries. ABD Maestro is targeting over ₹100 crore in FY27 across 11 states.

qa_highlights.question: Will leverage stretch with accelerated capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex funded by internal accruals and borrowing; management does not intend to breach covenants.

qa_highlights.question: Why are OC Blue and SRB7 declining and when do they return to growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Both are over 10 years old in competitive segments. Management is resetting A&P and packaging, with SRB7 showing low single-digit growth in test markets.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 300 bps gross margin expansion comes from backward integration?
qa_highlights.answer: About 30 bps in FY27 from the PET unit; the rest is price increases, trade-spend control and brand mix.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory days rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Proactive scotch buying ahead of rupee depreciation against the pound, stored under FTWZ, plus smaller-batch ABD Maestro production.

risks_watch: West Asia conflict driving input cost and export disruption; Q1 and early Q2 FY27 margin pressure.
Telangana price hike timing and Karnataka slab policy implementation.
Officer's Choice Blue and SRB7 decline; success of Q2 FY27 OC Blue relaunch.
Rising leverage during capex cycle (net debt/EBITDA 1.7x vs 2x ceiling); ESOP cost from FY27.
Execution of malt, ENA and UP bottling projects against H1 FY27 and H2 timelines; leadership transition announcement.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term margin and premiumisation targets, but candid that Q1 and early Q2 FY27 margins will be pressured. Answers on Karnataka and Telangana timing were hedged ('conservative but optimistic'), and the leadership-transition answer was brief.
key_quotes: So, the guidance that we are giving is that the FY27 overall margins, we should be hold on to the FY26, if not better it.
ABDM will not necessarily move the volume growth lever, but it substantially impacts the value growth lever.
Our entire capex investment will be a combination of internal accruals and borrowing whenever required, but we do not intend breaching these covenants at all.

growth.why: FY27 consolidated top-line growth guided to mid-teens (~15%) and FY27 EBITDA margin held at least at FY26's 14.4%, backed by Phase 1 PET plant, the Telangana malt distillery (H1 FY27), price increases, and backward integration, but no order book or hard volume numbers were given.
